title: Wendell and the Veil
premise: Mirabel Quintana has spent her life carving bones in the valley of Hollowmere, where the Veil — a dead god's last spell — mutes all magic, including the gift that lets her hear the dead. When the usurper King Aldric's witch-hunters breach the valley hunting the rumored 'last gifted,' Mirabel flees with a dying soldier, Cassian, who carries proof that Aldric's power is stolen from the imprisoned god behind the Veil. Their journey to the free cities forces Mirabel to choose between silencing the dead forever (the price of survival Aldric offers her) and carrying their testimony into a war that will demand the Veil be broken — unleashing both the god and every magic the world has suppressed for three centuries. In the end, Mirabel breaks the Veil not to free the god but to let the dead speak at Aldric's trial, accepting that she will lose her own gift and Cassian, who dies holding the valley's gate open; the book closes with her returning to Hollowmere, deaf to the dead for the first time, learning to live with silence.
about_author: Rafael Joubert is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist from Lyon who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed remains before turning to fiction. Their work blends quiet grief with high fantasy, and Wendell and the Veil is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet Hollowmere, where the Veil dampens magic, and Mirabel's secret: even here, faintly, she hears the dead through the bones she carves. She carves a memorial bell for a drowned child, hiding her gift from her superstitious neighbors. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment — she believes the valley protects her.

chapters.title: Wendell
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A wounded crown soldier, Cassian Wendell, collapses at her door pursued by witch-hunters; the Veil failed to stop them because they carry a shard of the god's bone. He carries sealed orders proving Aldric's armies march on the free cities. The hunters burn a neighboring farm asking questions. Emotional beat: terror shattering her illusion of safety.

chapters.title: What the Bones Said
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. To save Cassian she uses her gift fully for the first time, letting a dead hunter's bones reveal the hunt's true scope: lists of names, valleys mapped, her own village on them. They flee north by night as the hunters return. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve — leaving means abandoning everyone she loves to save strangers.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Silence
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Outside the Veil, magic floods back, and Mirabel is overwhelmed by the roar of the dead everywhere. Cassian, who lost his brother to Aldric's purges, teaches her to shield herself while wrestling with his orders: deliver the documents, trust no one gifted. Emotional beat: wary tenderness between two people using each other as shields.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the river city of Vasse, passage costs more than coin: the ferryman demands a bone carved by gifted hands to ward his plague-ridden docks. Helping him exposes Mirabel to a spy for the hunt. First glimpse of the free cities' decay and complicity. Emotional beat: the price of kindness in a world that punishes it.

chapters.title: Court of Ash
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. In the free city of Ardenne, Cassian delivers the documents to the Council — who already knew, and plan to bargain with Aldric rather than fight. Cassian is branded a deserter for fleeing with the truth instead of reporting it quietly. Emotional beat: disillusionment; duty revealed as theater, and love beginning to outweigh it.

chapters.title: The God Beneath
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The dead lead Mirabel to the Veil's anchor beneath Ardenne: the god Ossuar, imprisoned and half-mad, whose stolen power fuels Aldric's crown. The dead beg her to break the Veil and free them to testify. Aldric's hunters storm the city. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror — every path forward demands an unbearable price.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The city falls street by street; Cassian chooses treason openly to get Mirabel to the anchor, and the Council's bargain collapses when Aldric's envoy demands Mirabel's head personally. Cassian is gravely wounded covering her escape underground. Emotional beat: love declared in the grammar of sacrifice, with no promise of tomorrow.

chapters.title: Breaking the Veil
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the anchor, Ossuar offers her survival: keep her gift, walk away, let the world burn slowly. Instead she shatters the Veil — releasing the dead as witnesses across the land, stripping Aldric's stolen power mid-battle above, and severing her own hearing forever. Cassian dies holding the tunnel against the hunters. Emotional beat: climax as grief and triumph fused into one act.

chapters.title: The Sound of Silence
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Months later: Aldric stands trial, convicted by the testimony of the dead he silenced; the free cities rebuild uneasily in a world where magic has returned. Mirabel returns to Hollowmere, buries Cassian beneath the memorial bells, and picks up her carving tools — hands that make beauty without voices in them. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into peace; survival was never the prize, but living is.
